messages.text: 'They need a reset' - Has trust broken down between Hamilton, Ferrari pit wall?

metadata.summary: Ferrari's strategy decisions and communication with their drivers came under fresh scrutiny at the Singapore Grand Prix after Lewis Hamilton overrode a call to pit.
metadata.content: Lewis Hamilton: Has trust broken down between Ferrari driver and team's pit wall after Singapore GP issues? | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Opinion Lewis Hamilton: Has trust broken down between Ferrari driver and team's pit wall after Singapore GP issues? Listen to the latest episode of The F1 Show podcast as Simon Lazenby, Bernie Collins and Karun Chandhok look back at all the big talking points from the Singapore Sprint weekend; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1 Wednesday 14 October 2026 17:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins considers whether Lewis Hamilton has lost trust in Ferrari after overriding a team strategy call in Singapore Ferrari's strategy decisions and communication with their drivers came under fresh scrutiny at the Singapore Grand Prix after Lewis Hamilton overrode a call to pit. Hamilton finished finish sixth instead of a likely third in last Sunday's race after not heeding a call from the team's pit wall to stop under a lap-39 Virtual Safety Car. On team radio after the race following his struggle on worn tyres, Hamilton apologised for "my call" around the strategy, a position he subsequently reiterated on social media when he admitted he had learned a "painful lesson" by choosing "a strategy that ultimately didn't deliver". messages.text: Six Kings Slam tournament in Saudi Arabia postponed until December

metadata.summary: Tennis' big-money Six Kings Slam tournament in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia has been postponed from October to December due to unrest in the Middle East.
metadata.content: Six Kings Slam: Big-money tournament in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia postponed until December | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Six Kings Slam: Big-money tournament in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia postponed until December Decision to postpone Six King Slam follows continued unrest in Middle East and recent bombing of international airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh; tournament moved from October to December; you can watch the ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports Tennis Wednesday 14 October 2026 16:23, UK Image: The Six Kings Slam tournament in Saudi Arabia, which pays its winner £4.6m, has been postponed Tennis' big-money Six Kings Slam tournament in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia has been postponed from October to December due to unrest in the Middle East. The tournament, which is in its third edition and awards £1.2m per competing player and an extra £3.5m for the winner, was originally scheduled for October 21-24, but has now been moved to December 27-30. The six players included for 2026 are Carlos Alcaraz, Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur and Learner Tien. The decision to postpone follows continued unrest in the Middle East and the recent bombing of the international airport in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh.
